A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {P, \le}$ be a [[Definition:Non-Empty Set|non-empty]] [[Definition:Ordered Set|partially ordered set]] in which every [[Definition:Chain (Order Theory)|chain]] has an [[Definition:Upper Bound of Set|upper bound]].
Then $P$ has a [[Definition:Maximal Element|maximal element]].

B_source.statement: To exhaust a set, build an increasing sequence by [[Principle of Transfinite Recursion|transfinite recursion]], choosing a new element at each stage, until no choice remains.

substitutions.the stage-by-stage construction: an increasing chain indexed by the ordinals
substitutions.the choice made at each stage: a strict upper bound of the chain built so far
substitutions.the point where the process halts: the stage at which no strict upper bound exists

derived.the process must terminate: it cannot inject the ordinals into a set, so some stage admits no strict upper bound
derived.the final object: an element with no element strictly above it, that is, a maximal element

validity_conditions: Choosing a strict upper bound at each stage requires the axiom of choice, which is why Zorn's lemma is equivalent to it rather than provable outright.
The chain hypothesis is what supplies an upper bound at limit stages, where there is no immediate predecessor to extend from.
Termination follows from replacement: an unbounded construction would inject a proper class of ordinals into a set, which is impossible.
proof_plan:
{{AimForCont}} $P$ has no maximal element.
Using a [[Definition:Choice Function|choice function]], build $\family {p_\alpha}$ by [[Principle of Transfinite Recursion|transfinite recursion]], choosing at each successor stage a strict upper bound of $p_\alpha$.
At a limit stage $\lambda$, $\set {p_\alpha: \alpha < \lambda}$ is a chain, so has an upper bound; choose a strict upper bound of it.

The construction gives an [[Definition:Injection|injection]] from the class of all [[Definition:Ordinal|ordinals]] into the set $P$.
By [[Hartogs' Lemma (Set Theory)|Hartogs' Lemma]], this is impossible.
